findings.claim_or_location: Bibliography ref [20] (PMID: 22574274), grounding finding 13/14 — the load-bearing prescription-stimulant risk-floor / PRESCRIPTIVE_DIRECTIVE boundary claims (Schedule II status, dependence/cardiovascular liabilities, ~1.9% nonmedical prevalence).
findings.issue: PMID 22574274 is MISATTRIBUTED. That PMID resolves to Pang Y et al. (2012), 'Neuron-oligodendrocyte myelination co-culture derived from embryonic rat spinal cord and cerebral cortex,' Brain Behav — an unrelated in-vitro rat methods paper. It is NOT Lakhan SE & Kirchgessner A's 'Prescription stimulants in individuals with and without ADHD: misuse, cognitive impact, and adverse effects.' The cited DOI (10.1002/brb3.78), journal (Brain and Behavior), year (2012), and byline are all correct and resolve to the intended paper; only the PMID is wrong. Per rubric, a wrong PMID on the load-bearing risk-floor citation is a CRITICAL/HALT-level citation-fidelity defect even though the underlying claim is sound and the fix is mechanical.
findings.recommended_fix: Correct the PMID for ref [20] from 22574274 to 23139911 (verified correct PMID for Lakhan SE & Kirchgessner A, Brain Behav 2012;2(5):661-77, DOI 10.1002/brb3.78). No change to the finding-13/14 claims is required.

findings.issue: Byline is incomplete: the section cites 'James JE.' as sole author, but PubMed lists two authors — Jack E James and Peter J Rogers. The PMID, DOI, title, journal, year, and the quoted 'almost wholly attributable to reversal of adverse withdrawal effects' conclusion all verify correctly; only the byline is truncated.
findings.recommended_fix: Update the byline for ref [2] to 'James JE, Rogers PJ.' to match the source record.
